steps.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, salt, and sugar. Mix well, then cut in shortening until mixture resembles coarse meal.

In a small bowl, combine egg, vinegar, and 4 tablespoons of water. Whisk together, then add gradually to flour mixture, stirring with a fork. Mix until dough forms a ball. Add one more tablespoon of water if necessary.
Allow dough to rest in refrigerator 10 minutes before rolling out.

raw_recipe.headline: French Pastry Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: This recipe makes a sweet dough that is perfect for fruit pies or tarts. A bit of sugar, an egg and vinegar make this dough different from the traditional, but the end result is pastry that is manageable and flaky. Try adding a bit of lemon zest if you 're feeling adventurous.

review.reviewBody: This crust was great! Great flavor even though it doesn't have any butter in it.(I'm a true butter lover) And it has a great texture, tender and flaky. The key is to not over work it. When I added the liquids and stirred with a fork to get everything somewhat mixed, I then dumped the dough onto a piece of cling wrap where I used it to lightly squeeze it together until it formed a nice ball. If you knead this dough too much it flatten all the shortening pieces. Therefore you won't have anymore flaky, just tough. The cling wrap trick also helps in not adding extra flour as you do when you knead, and that can also make a tough dough.

Look no further!! This is the ultimate pie crust to use for every pie you make!! I worried about this recipe not having butter, and choose to use another recipe that used all butter at first. Big mistake! Crust was tough and not flaky at all. So on the next pie I used this recipe and wow!!!!!!!! It was flaky and melted in my mouth!!!!!!!! I made it my own for a peach pie by substituting 1/4 cup of the flour with ground walnuts (ground to powder using a spice grinder) and then using brown sugar instead of white sugar. For the shortening I used butter crisco that had spent the night before in the freezer. Just before baking, I took another reviewers suggestion and brushed with an egg white only egg wash, and sprinkled with a sugar cinnamon mixture. The result was a pefect crust with a spectacular glaze and the taste was fantastic!!!!! I could seriously eat the whole pan of crust by myself and will definately never buy store bought crust again! This is my go to secret pie crust now. Try it, you wont regret.

I make it in my food processor, using the pluse to control the length. You only want to process until it just starts to come together. I also sometimes use frozen European butter instead of Crisco and a splash of vodka instead of vinegar. I was told by a french pastry chef that vodka helps the flakiness. Just made six of these and wrapped them in parchment paper, put them in the fridge, and will bake my pies tomorrow. Definately worth the effort!!

I used this recipe to make mini mincemeat tarts and it was great! I used butter rather than shortening. I also used the suggestion of putting the dough ball in a plastic ziplock bag and stuck it in the freezer for 10 minutes. After taking out, I cut the sides of the bag and rolled the dough sandwich. It worked really well. I will definitely use this recipe again. Delicious!

Great results. I used butter instead of shortening. I would guess that leaf lard, or a blend of lard and butter would make this even better.

This recipe makes two pie crusts. One for the bottom of the tin and one for the top of the pie. After you mix and gently knead the dough together, divide into two balls before putting in the fridge.

This is the BEST pie crust recipe EVER! I've used it to make my apple pies and chocolate sawdust pies every holiday season for 6 years now!. The recipe calls for shortening, but I prefer to substitute 1 cup unsalted butter instead, for flavor. Either way, it's always a great result. If you choose to use butter, try grating the cold butter into your dry ingredients. This prevents any big clumps, and you won't have to work the dough as much to mix it, so the end product is has a better, flakier texture and taste. Always use the 5th tablespoon of water, and a brush of egg-wash on top makes the most gorgeous, golden-brown presentation! Try it. Love it. Save it.

Made it in the food processor. Pulsed off and on for about a minute give or take. Popped it in the fridge for 10 minutes then rolled it out and put it in the pie pan. For CREAM PIE - Blind bake at 425° with aluminum foil & dry beans (to hold its shape) for 12 minutes. Removed the beans/foil and baked for another 15 minutes until golden. Brushed on egg wash and baked for another 3 minutes. Pop in the freezer for another 10 minutes to cool before adding cream pie filling. Perfection! Thank you!

I made this and used it to make an apple pie for my sons 37th birthday - he’s not a cake fan - this crust is SO GOOD! The only change to it that I made, was to substitute unsalted butter in place of the shortening. I did use my food processor like another reviewer on here suggested and it made it so fast. It turned out perfect and the crust has really good flavor, everyone loved it! I had another crust on here that I used and loved (and will still use) but I wanted to try this one also. It’s equally as fabulous. I’m really glad I tried this one. Thanks to the submitter of this recipe, for sharing it!

I have used this recipe for lots of years and it turns out every time. I sometimes use unsalted butter, butter Crisco, lard. I use this recipe for pot pies, fruit pies, savory pies. For savory pies, omit the sugar. I also use a food processor for the dry ingredients and shortening and then mix in the wet.

I love to bake but I have never been able to totally "master" a pie crust. Something always goes wrong. We got our hands on a huge bunch of fresh picked farm cherries and I really could just taste a cherry pie - although I feared my usual crust failure. I took a stab at this, I chilled lard, and used a farm fresh egg from one of my lovely chooks. This was the BEST pie our family has ever eaten, at least made by me and not Marie Calendar. :) I would have never thought you could get a crust like this without butter. I was afraid of the vinegar too, but it is magic. I was careful to barely work the dough together, I put the crust back in the fridge for a while before baking my beautiful cherry pie. MMMMMMMMM I can still smell that baking in the oven!! yum. A KEEPER!!

I have used this recipe many times. The only thing that I have changed is the amount of water used. I have always needed to add a great deal more to make the dough manageable. I prefer a soft dough that I can roll out with just minor additions of flour. It has turned out great! If I am short on shortening, which provides a flakier crust, I have mixed in coconut oil. That has added a unique pleasant flavor.
This has become my go to pie crust recipe.

This recipe is perfect. I actually use butter instead of shortening and only 1 tsp of sugar since I don’t like a very sweet crust. It also works for quiche or savory pies this way. I only need 4 tbsp water.
Hands down the best pie crust I’ve ever had.
Very good and easy to make
Really flaky and delicious.
Use butter or at least half butter and half shortening. Real food is butter is better
Awesome!!! Love this recipe
Simple to make. Works great

diferent then other crusts I have mede....very flaky like French pastry on the top pf there and tender on the bottom of the pie where the fruit sits. I was a little worried because when put together there appeared little balls of butter. I didn't want to handle it too much as this ruins a cruse..lt worked out and was a winner... The top of the pie was a little more crispy than I am used to but every loved the pie....now I saw a mushroom pastry in a local store that I may try and use this recipe....perfect
